newsitem.title: UK: London palladium fixes at new all-time high.
newsitem.headline: London palladium fixes at new all-time high.

text.p: Palladium was fixed at a fresh highest-ever level on Wednesday amid escalating supply concerns, while platinum fixed at a new 16-month high.
Palladium was fixed at $210.00, its highest level since fixings began in 1989. Platinum was set at $425.00 an ounce, the highest since February 7, 1996.
The price of palladium, a rare white metal used in electronics, catalytic converters and dentistry, started soaring at the end of last year because of supply delays from key producer Russia.
Prices careered to a high bid of $218 an ounce on Wednesday morning, the highest level since 1980, as dealers scrambled to buy and borrow the metal in a very tight market, traders said.
By contrast, palladium had ended at $193.00/$197.00 on Tuesday in London, while platinum had finished at $415.00/$419.00.
Severe volatility is expected to continue in platinum and palladium markets until Russian suppliers and Japanese consumers clinch long-delayed supply deals, traders added.
